title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi-tool and parallel calls
author: Claire Zhang
description:
Context: Operators and product teams have asked for clearer semantics and safer ergonomics around tool/function calls: parallel tool invocation, deterministic injection of tool results into subsequent tool inputs and the model context, and robust retry behavior for transient tool failures. This PR introduces an execution ergonomics layer to the tool-runner and OpenAI-compat shim to make multi-tool workflows easier to author and more reliable.
Motivation: Many real-world tool chains are naturally parallel and/or contain non-idempotent tools. Previously we either ran tools serially (too slow) or allowed ad-hoc parallelism with poor retry semantics and inconsistent context injection. This caused streaming instability and made OpenAI-compat consumers implement brittle workarounds.
Summary of changes:
- Add a ToolExecutionCoordinator that schedules multi-tool and parallel execution, applies idempotency tokens, and records deterministic result slots for injection into follow-up calls.
- Implement ParallelExecutor with request-scoped batching and backoff-aware retry for transient tool errors.
- Extend the OpenAI compatibility layer: function_call responses now include a "tool_execution" metadata object with execution_id, attempt_count, and result_slot references. Old clients continue to receive the original function_call schema unless the feature flag is enabled.
- Streaming stability fixes: chunked tool outputs now stream through the same tokenization guard used by LLM responses to avoid framing issues; large tool outputs are automatically truncated with summary hints and stored in result slots for follow-up requests.
- SDK changes and docs: update python SDK shim and docs for new execution semantics and examples for parallel tool patterns.
Checklist:
- [x] Add coordinator and parallel executor implementation
- [x] Add idempotency token plumbing and retry policy
- [x] OpenAI-compat extension with opt-in behavior via feature flag (toolExec.v2)
- [x] Streaming stability fixes and e2e tests
- [x] Docs + SDK examples updated
Commits summary:
- Implement ToolExecutionCoordinator and unit tests
- Add ParallelExecutor and exponential-backoff retry logic
- Extend openai_compat to emit tool_execution metadata and maintain old behavior behind feature flag
- Streaming fixes: guardrails for chunked tool output and large-result truncation
- Docs: examples and migration notes
Changed areas/files (high level): redwood/serving/tool_runner.py (coordinator + runner refs), redwood/serving/runner/parallel_executor.py (new executor), redwood/api/streaming.py (stream framing guards), redwood/openai_compat.py (compat shim updates), redwood-sdk-python/openai_compat.py (shim + examples), redwood-tests/test-tool-calls.py (integration + flaky-case coverage), docs/api/tool-calling.md (migration guide + examples). How to review:
- Review the coordinator/parallel executor for race conditions and locking semantics
- Validate idempotency token propagation across retries and across the OpenAI-compat layer
- Run e2e tests with the feature flag enabled and disabled to ensure backwards compatibility
- Validate streaming scenarios with large outputs (see test tool-call-large-output)
Backwards compatibility and rollout:
- Default behavior is unchanged. The new behavior is gated by the feature flag toolExec.v2. Ops can enable per-customer or globally.
- Migration guide added to docs/api/tool-calling.md with examples for multi-tool parallel patterns and recommended idempotency best practices.
QA and testing:
- Added unit tests for coordinator scheduling logic and deterministic result slot assignment
- Added flaky-case integration tests to exercise retry behavior against a mock tool that fails N-1 times
- End-to-end tests to assert OpenAI-compat shim emits tool_execution metadata when enabled
Notes: This is targeted for a gradual rollout to dedicated/private customers first to observe production tool patterns before global enablement.

release_notes: Improved tool-calling ergonomics: opt-in parallel tool execution, deterministic result injection slots, and safer retry semantics. Streaming stability for chunked tool output. Feature gated behind toolExec.v2; see docs/api/tool-calling.md for migration and examples.
